solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Detective grabs theatrical chaps making secret escape

indicators.note: the detective takes hold of the other pieces, so they sit inside his letters

parts.note: camp means exaggeratedly theatrical
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A police officer seizes some flamboyant actors who are trying to slip away unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Decamping is leaving suddenly, often quietly, so the act of doing so is a stealthy getaway.

clue.text: I am pro the termination of some dreadful stores

indicators.note: the termination of a word is its final letter
dreadful suggests something badly made, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone declares support for closing down a few awful shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the termination of some' gives E; with IAMPRO that makes IAMPROE, which 'dreadful' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large shop, and its plural names several such retail outlets.

clue.text: Give out set of books, missing out none of them

parts.note: leaving none out means taking all
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone hands out a set of books, making sure every volume goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is written in answer order whatever the clue's order: the 'all' piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion shares among people.

clue.text: Address concern when provision depends on chance?

definitions.text: Address concern when provision depends on chance?

parts.words: Address concern when provision depends on chance?
parts.note: a worry tied to where you live, when the services you receive depend on the luck of your location

explanation.surface: A worry about where you live, in a world where what you get is down to luck.
explanation.walkthrough: A POSTCODE LOTTERY is the British complaint that public services such as healthcare vary by area; a postcode is a UK postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names unequal provision of public services decided by the district where someone happens to reside.

clue.text: Oral exam — tick man off!

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, as food goes off, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cry to a teacher: mark the spoken test, or give the man a telling-off!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an angry exclamation, ending with the very sign it spells.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation sign ends a shouted or emphatic utterance, like the rebuke the clue itself finishes with.

clue.text: One's spouted at the meal table

definitions.text: One's spouted at the meal table

parts.words: One's spouted at the meal table
parts.note: spouted suggests talking at length at dinner, but this vessel literally has a spout and pours there

explanation.surface: Someone holding forth tediously over dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot with a spout, used for pouring a brew at the table at mealtimes.

clue.text: Horses are needed for this explorer

definitions.meaning: a team sport played on horseback with mallets
Marco ..., the Venetian traveller to China

explanation.surface: An explorer whose expedition depends on having horses.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the mounted ball game; the other is the medieval Venetian traveller Marco.

clue.text: Being rich, one lets up foolishly

indicators.note: acting foolishly is acting without sense, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wealthy person carelessly relaxes their effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenteous means abundant or copious, the state of having riches in plenty.

clue.text: See 4
Old china that is glittery with many colours

definitions.text: that is glittery with many colours

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

explanation.surface: Some antique porcelain that sparkles in many hues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like porcelain; it is cockney rhyming slang, china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: This gemstone shows a play of iridescent colours, sparkling in many shades.

clue.text: Escort a man abused in US city

indicators.note: something abused is mistreated and knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is mistreated by an escort somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of California, a city in the United States.

clue.text: Judge starts to castigate rogue, getting one twitching

indicators.note: the starts of the two words are their opening letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: A magistrate begins scolding a villain, who develops a nervous twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer judges the merits of works, so a critic is an assessor.

clue.text: Followers given job with drinks all round

indicators.note: the drinks surround the job, so its letters sit inside

parts.note: ales are drinks of beer
a post is a job

explanation.surface: Supporters given employment, with a round of drinks for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve disciples were followers of Jesus, and the word extends to any devoted supporters.

clue.text: Country river — help old boy to get back to it

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: getting back means going in reverse, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: aid means help
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An old man helped back to the river in some country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get back' reverses AIDOB to BODIA, which is joined to the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in Southeast Asia, whose capital is Phnom Penh.

clue.text: Part of the company building is cleaner when Dora's worked inside it

indicators.note: the reworked name goes within the cleaner's letters

parts.note: a broom is a cleaning tool

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaner named Dora works in an office building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaner' looks like Dora's job; it is the broom she ends up inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The room where a firm's directors meet is one area of its premises.

clue.text: Beast making comeback in sexy romance

indicators.note: making comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An animal returns to a steamy love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The run XYRO sits inside 'sexy romance'; 'in' signals it and 'making comeback' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large straight-horned antelope of Africa and Arabia, an animal.

clue.text: Most raucous quarrel fades over time

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the next

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
dies means fades away

explanation.surface: The noisiest argument dies down as time passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdy means noisy and disorderly, and this is its superlative form.

clue.text: Whale involved in major catastrophe

indicators.note: the letters are wrapped up within the phrase, spanning its two words

explanation.surface: A whale caught up in a huge disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale, a large black-and-white toothed marine mammal.

clue.text: Ox not unknown to get stuck in crag — or some other animal

indicators.note: the shortened ox is lodged within the crag's letters

parts.note: a crag is a rock

indicators.note: not says the unknown is dropped from the ox

parts.note: a zebu is a humped ox
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An ox wedged on a rocky outcrop, or perhaps a different creature.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebu is the humped ox of India; Z is an algebraic unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: A male roe deer, a different animal from the ox in the surface.

clue.text: Very brave man in club team

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A courageous player in a club's squad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironside was a nickname for a man of great bravery and toughness, as Edmund Ironside or Cromwell.

clue.text: Rebuffs from Stormy Daniels?

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: Refusals from Stormy Daniels, the American adult-film actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' reads as part of the name; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a refusal or rejection, so these are rebuffs.

clue.text: Sweet child — dad's favourite

parts.note: pop is a word for dad
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A lovely child who is their father's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet is an affectionate term for a dear little child or darling.

clue.text: Bit of money, two old pence now chucked or put away

parts.note: a sen is a small coin of Japan and elsewhere
d was the symbol for an old British penny, so two give DD

indicators.note: chucked means thrown about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some coins, a couple of pre-decimal pennies, now thrown away or saved.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 the British penny was written d; a sen is a small Japanese coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To send down is British for to jail someone, the same as putting them away.

clue.text: At year's end hospital department is in good order

parts.note: Dec is December, the year's final month
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: By December the hospital unit is running properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent can mean satisfactory or respectable, in a proper and acceptable state.

clue.text: Length of old copper piece

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A section of antique copper.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient unit of measure, based on the forearm, used in former times.

clue.text: Fat couple troubled about nothing seen as inappropriate

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the zero
troubled means disturbed, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A large pair is upset over nothing, behaving improperly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not in its proper position or setting is unsuitable or improper.

clue.text: Venerable man said to provide this aid to prayer?

indicators.note: said signals the word is spoken, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: the Venerable Bede was an English monk and historian

explanation.surface: A holy old man is reputed to supply this help for praying.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosary beads are counted through the fingers while saying prayers.

clue.text: Hastily read second novel by Kipling

parts.note: Kim is a novel by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: Someone races through a Kipling novel for the second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim a text is to glance over it quickly without careful study.

clue.text: Provide a lift prior to work or lecture

indicators.note: prior says the first piece comes before the others

parts.note: to take someone is to give them a lift somewhere
a task is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Offer someone a ride before going to the office or to give a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To scold someone at length is to reprimand them, the sense of giving a lecture.
